name: Parallel Computing
summary: Take the same computation from one CPU core to threads, OpenMP, SIMD, a GPU, and a cluster. Keep the result correct. Understand the execution model. Measure what actually changed.

startHere.title: How to use this course
startHere.covers: Read one page, then do the short exercise on that page.

startHere.title: The list of numbers we keep reusing
startHere.covers: One list of integers is the example for the whole course.

chapters.label: Parallel Thinking
chapters.question: What does it mean to run work at the same time?
lessons: A program is a list of steps
Why one core stops being enough

chapters.label: CPU
chapters.question: How does a CPU run multiple pieces of work?

chapters.label: OpenMP
chapters.question: How do we parallelize loops without manually managing every thread?

chapters.label: Algorithms
chapters.question: Which algorithms are naturally parallel?
chapters.covers: Map, reduce, histogram, stencil, scan, sort.

chapters.label: SIMD
chapters.question: What if one instruction processes several values?
chapters.covers: Vector lanes, vectorization, alignment, SIMD + threads.

chapters.label: GPU
chapters.question: What changes when thousands of workers execute on a device?
chapters.covers: GPU execution, memory, kernels, CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, Vulkan.

chapters.label: Distributed
chapters.question: What happens when workers do not share memory?

chapters.label: Measuring
chapters.question: Did we actually make the program faster?
chapters.covers: Timing, speedup, efficiency, Amdahl's law, bandwidth, cache, profiling.
